A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VAR research despite the changed title. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching of retained, revised, and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original HHA alignment experiments, generative-benchmark results, training analyses, batch-size ablations, and generated-response examples.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds GRPO comparisons, conversational-benchmark outcomes, partition-estimator analyses, and computational measurements.

M1.justification: The specified training rule changes substantially. v1 Equation 21 and Algorithm 1 include the reference-policy probability in each sample's weight and use a summed normalizer; v3 Equations 9–10 and Algorithm 1 omit that numerator factor and average the normalizer. v3 also specifies gradient descent on a positive weighted log-likelihood, whereas v1 supplies a negative-log loss. These are substantive changes to the printed procedure; implementation changes are not established.

E1.justification: v3 adds general conversational evaluation on AlpacaEval 2.0 and Arena-Hard 0.1, substantially extending evaluation beyond the retained HHA and knowledge, mathematics, coding, and reasoning benchmarks. OffsetBias and UltraFeedback training coverage remains unchanged. MT-Bench remains a judging protocol, not an added test dataset.

E2.justification: v3 newly evaluates online GRPO against VAR on Qwen2.5-3B and Llama3.2-3B in Table 4, adding an important online comparison absent from v1. Table 8 also introduces a computational comparison against SFT and DPO. The existing DPO and ALoL benchmark comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce length-controlled and ordinary conversational win rates, per-epoch time, throughput, peak memory, and dedicated reference-sampled estimation controls. The new Llama GRPO comparison explicitly uses SFT initialization, unlike its VAR counterpart. Existing HHA sampling, generation settings, and generative-benchmark shot counts remain unchanged; their implementation descriptions move from v1 Appendix C into the main text.

E4.justification: v3 adds a reference-sampled alternative to the batch-size ablation, compares offline and online partition-estimator variance across batch sizes, and measures computational overhead. These directly investigate estimator reliability and efficiency. The earlier training-stability plots, output-length analysis, original batch-size results, and case study are retained.

E5.justification: v3 Figure 4 newly reports partition-estimator variance, although the replication count used to estimate it is unspecified. Existing HHA reporting of means and standard errors across three seeds is unchanged and relocated from v1 Appendix C.1. Neither version establishes an increase in repeated training runs.

E6.justification: The original HHA tables and generative-benchmark scores are unchanged, but substantial new results appear. Table 6 reports DPO ahead on AlpacaEval length-controlled win rate, 8.73 versus VAR's 8.26, while VAR leads Arena-Hard, 10.8 versus 8.6. Other additions include GRPO results, estimator-variance curves, a reference-sampled ablation averaging 68.32 versus 68.42 in-batch, and computational profiles.

T1.justification: v3 replaces the ELBO-based development with an explicit forward/reverse-KL discussion, corrects the entropy sign in the KL decomposition, and revises the partition-estimation argument. It removes v1's negative-weight unboundedness theorem and proof, Theorem B.2, and the separate RLHF-consistency proof in Appendix D. The clipping analysis and positive-weight lower-bound theorem remain, reordered.

C1.justification: The abstract extends the contribution to matching or exceeding online methods while claiming over fivefold faster convergence than GRPO, an empirical claim absent from v1. It also introduces a claimed average 7.16% advantage over DPO. The central variational, positive-weighted-SFT alignment claim remains.

C2.justification: v3 adds benchmark-dependent qualifications from the mixed AlpacaEval/Arena-Hard findings and interprets the new variance and computational analyses as support for offline estimation. Appendix B explicitly limits validation to at most Qwen2.5-32B-Int4 and acknowledges inconsistent post-alignment performance. Existing reward-bias, output-length, and training-stability interpretations largely remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds a VAR code-repository link and discloses pre-shuffling fixed micro-batches, precomputing and storing cross-pair rewards, and using a frozen reference model during training. Most existing optimizer, hardware, decoding, and benchmark implementation details are simply relocated from v1 Appendix C. The PDFs do not establish that the newly disclosed preprocessing was newly implemented.

R1.justification: v3 adds positioning against reference-free SimPO and learned-reference alignment, and connects its supervised formulation to Wu et al.'s reward-rectification analysis. Variational-method background citations also expand. These extend the discussion while retaining the central positioning around ALoL and direct approximation of the RLHF optimum.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, and variational-method exposition are substantially rewritten. Motivation moves after the derivation, implementation details and Qwen win-rate discussion move from appendices into the main text, and experimental and appendix sections are reorganized. These constitute extensive narrative and structural revision beyond adding experiments.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to a single-column layout with redesigned headings and author information. v1 Figures 1 and 4 are combined into v3 Figure 1 using the retained plots. v3 adds comparison Tables 4, 6, and 8 and a new variance Figure 4, expands the ablation table, and relocates or resizes numerous existing displays.

improvement.justification: The new online comparisons, conversational tests, estimator analyses, and resource measurements strengthen empirical coverage, while preprocessing and code disclosures help reproducibility. However, v3 introduces an optimization-sign inconsistency in Algorithm 1. Its new Table 4 also repeats Qwen2.5-0.5B baseline values under Llama3.2-3B, conflicting with Table 1. The reported timings imply approximately 4.1-fold and 5.1-fold per-epoch speedups, providing limited support for the abstract's over-fivefold convergence claim. These benefits coexist with substantive new method and reporting inconsistencies, preventing a confident net-quality judgment.
